youtube.title: KARLEEN GRIBBLE
youtube.summary: Professor Karleen Gribble, an academic and researcher at Western Sydney University, speaks with Michael Arbon about the recording of sex in Australian health data and the risks of inaccurate records. They discuss the shift towards gender-neutral language in healthcare, its implications for medical safety and research and how replacing terms such as “women” and “mothers” may affect public health communication and support for mothers. Discover more from Karleen Gribble Discover more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with NZ First leader Winston Peters on the party’s election campaign, covering the Covid-19 vaccine rollout, puberty blockers, fuel security and domestic oil exploration. Winston defends merit-based recruitment over diversity, equity and inclusion policies, highlights his party’s economic expertise and calls for growth above 3%. He dismisses current polling as unreliable, predicting NZ First will surprise its critics on election night. youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart discuss election turnout, voter enrolment and misunderstandings about MMP, arguing for strategic voting to strengthen the current coalition. They examine the potential gains for ACT and New Zealand First, Labour’s handling of gang controversies and concerns about The Opportunities Party’s policies and censorship. youtube.title: NATHAN SURENDRAN
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with engineer Nathan Surendran, chair of the Wise Response Society, about how declining net energy returns and diesel supply pressures could reshape New Zealand’s economy. They discuss fuel conservation, local food production, rooftop solar and electrification as ways to build resilience, reduce reliance on fragile supply chains and ease cost-of-living pressures. Nathan also challenges the focus on government debt while highlighting the scale of private debt. Discover more from Nathan at Energy & Resilience on Substack and the Wise Response Society on Substack

youtube.title: SAM BAILEY
youtube.summary: Alistair Harding interviews Dr Sam Bailey about raising $250,000 in six days to pay costs and fines imposed following Medical Council disciplinary proceedings over her Covid-era publications. Sam discusses her case, the consequences of her bankruptcy proceedings and concerns about medical regulation and freedom of expression. She also calls on listeners to write to the Medical Council to end its persecution of Doctors and restore freedom of speech for the profession. youtube.title: LEGAL HUB
